hooks.text: Our entire galaxy is sliding toward a central gravitational focal point.
Why is our entire galaxy sliding like water down a valley?
Our home galaxy is not drifting aimlessly through empty space.

title: The Colossal Cosmic Drain Pulling Our Galaxy
description: Scientists mapping galaxy movements discovered that the Milky Way belongs to Laniakea, a supercluster where we are all sliding toward a single focal point.

beats.text: Our entire galaxy is sliding toward a central gravitational focal point.
beats.visual: Illustration of the Milky Way galaxy from a distant perspective, 2020

beats.text: For years, astronomers only mapped our cosmic neighbors using light-based positions.
beats.visual: Sloan Digital Sky Survey visualization of the cosmic web, 2009

beats.text: In September 2014, researcher R. Brent Tully tracked how these galaxies actually move.
beats.visual: Photograph of astronomer R. Brent Tully pointing at a stellar diagram, 2014

beats.text: Using the Green Bank Telescope, his team mapped a structure spanning 400 to 500 million light-years.
beats.visual: The Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope in West Virginia, 2015

beats.text: They named it Laniakea, a Hawaiian word meaning immense heaven or open skies.
beats.visual: Photograph of a traditional Polynesian voyaging canoe sailing on the ocean, 2012

beats.text: This supercluster contains approximately 100,000 galaxies, matching the mass of 100 quadrillion Suns.
beats.visual: Computer simulation of the Laniakea Supercluster boundaries, 2014

beats.text: Like water flowing down a valley, all these galaxies are sliding toward the Great Attractor.
beats.visual: Visualization of galactic flow paths curving toward the Great Attractor, 2014

beats.text: On the outskirts, our own Milky Way remains locked in this giant flow.
beats.visual: Stunning wide-field photograph of the Milky Way galaxy, 2018

better_than_last: Ensured Beat 2 and all other beats explicitly and strictly draw their facts from the research claims.
